title: Your first module
summary: A module is a folder of .tf files with inputs and outputs. Extract one from working code with moved blocks, then make several copies with for_each on the module call.

steps.title: A module is a folder
body: Every folder of `.tf` files is a **module**. The one you run `terraform` in is the **root module**; any folder it
calls with a `module` block is a **child module**. A reusable module has a conventional layout:
README.md      what it is for, an example call
source = "./modules/site"      # a local path, a registry address or a Git URL
domain = "shop.example.com"     # every other argument is one of its variables
Inside the module, resources only see the module's own variables, locals and resources: everything it needs comes
in as a variable, everything the caller needs goes out as an output. That boundary is the point. Resource

steps.prompt: Why should a reusable module have `required_providers` but no `provider "aws" { region = ... }` block?
options: The caller configures providers (region, credentials, aliases) and passes them in; a provider block inside also stops the module from being used with count, for_each or depends_on
Provider blocks are not allowed in files called main.tf
It makes the module faster to init
Only the registry may configure providers
steps.explain: A module that configures its own provider decides the region and credentials for every caller, and cannot be repeated with `for_each`: *Module is incompatible with count, for_each, and depends_on*. Declare what you need in `required_providers`; let the root module configure it. This module's boss has that bug.

steps.title: Extract a module, destroy nothing
prompt: `~/infra/web/main.tf` sets up one site (`shop.example.com`): a TLS key, a self-signed certificate and an nginx server
block. The docs site needs the same. First, move the shop's resources into a module, without changing anything real:
1. Create `modules/site` with `main.tf` (the three resources, using `var.domain` instead of `shop.example.com`),
`variables.tf` (a typed, described `domain`), `outputs.tf` (an output `cert_pem` with the certificate) and
2. Replace the root's `main.tf` with a call: `module "shop"` with `source = "./modules/site"`.
3. Add `moved` blocks so the plan says *has moved to* three times and nothing else. `terraform init` (a new module

checks.name: the resources live in module.shop
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/web && terraform state list | sort | tr '\n' ' '
checks.fail: `terraform state list` should show the three resources under `module.shop.` and nothing in the root.

checks.name: the certificate was not replaced
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/web && terraform state show -no-color module.shop.tls_self_signed_cert.site | grep -q "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/cert)"
checks.fail: The certificate is a new one (its serial number changed): it was destroyed and re-created. Press Reset scenario and use `moved` blocks.

checks.name: the module has its files
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/web/modules/site && grep -q 'variable "domain"' variables.tf && grep -q 'output "cert_pem"' outputs.tf && grep -q 'required_providers' versions.tf && grep -q 'var.domain' main.tf && ! grep -q 'shop.example.com' main.tf && ! grep -q '^provider' *.tf
checks.fail: `modules/site` needs `main.tf` (using `var.domain`, no hard-coded `shop.example.com`), `variables.tf` with `domain`, `outputs.tf` with `cert_pem` and `versions.tf` with `required_providers` (and no `provider` block).

hints: `mkdir -p modules/site && cp main.tf modules/site/main.tf && cp versions.tf modules/site/`, then in the module replace `"shop.example.com"` with `var.domain` (and `shop.example.com` inside strings with `${var.domain}`).
The root's `main.tf` becomes just `module "shop" { source = "./modules/site"  domain = "shop.example.com" }`. Run `terraform init` so Terraform sees the module.
`moved { from = tls_private_key.site  to = module.shop.tls_private_key.site }`, and the same for `tls_self_signed_cert.site` and `local_file.nginx`.
steps.explain: The plan: three *has moved to* notes, `0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. Extracting a module is a refactor like a rename, and it needs the same care: in a real cloud account, forgetting the `moved` blocks would have replaced the certificate (and the load balancer using it would have served an error for a while).

steps.title: Many copies: for_each on the module
body: A `module` block takes `count` and `for_each` like a resource. Every instance is a full copy of the module:
value = { for d, m in module.site : d => m.cert_pem }   # module.site is a map of instances
Addresses become `module.site["shop.example.com"].tls_private_key.site`. Going from a single `module "shop"` to
the keyed form is one more `moved` block, for the whole module at once:

steps.title: Add the docs site
prompt: `~/infra/web` now calls `module "shop"`. Replace it with one `module "site"` that uses `for_each` over
`shop.example.com` and `docs.example.com` (`domain = each.key`), move the shop's existing instance into it so its
certificate is kept, and apply. Add an output `certs`: a map from domain to `cert_pem`.

checks.name: both sites exist, keyed by domain
checks.fail: `terraform state list` should show three resources under `module.site["shop.example.com"]` and three under `module.site["docs.example.com"]`.

checks.name: the shop kept its certificate
checks.fail: The shop's certificate was replaced. Press Reset scenario and add `moved { from = module.shop  to = module.site["shop.example.com"] }`.

checks.name: the certs output
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/web && terraform output -json certs | jq -r 'keys | join(",")' && terraform output -json certs | jq -e 'all(.[]; startswith("-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"))' >/dev/null
checks.fail: `terraform output -json certs` should map both domains to a PEM certificate.

checks.name: plan is clean
checks.fail: Apply: `terraform plan` should show no changes and `out/docs.example.com/nginx.conf` should exist.

hints: One `moved` block moves the whole module instance: `from = module.shop`, `to = module.site["shop.example.com"]`. Remove (or replace) the old `moved` blocks that point at `module.shop.*`, or point them at the new address.
The output: `value = { for d, m in module.site : d => m.cert_pem }`. Then `terraform init`, plan, apply.
solution: value = { for d, m in module.site : d => m.cert_pem }
steps.explain: Plan: the shop's module instance *has moved to* `module.site["shop.example.com"]`, and three resources are created for docs. Adding a third site is now one string in the set. Keys are domains, so removing one site never disturbs another.

steps.prompt: Order the steps of extracting resources into a module safely.
lines: write the module folder (variables, main, outputs, versions)
replace the resources in the root with a module call
add one moved block per resource
terraform plan: only has moved to, 0 to add, 0 to destroy
steps.explain: `init` is needed whenever a module call is added or its `source` changes: it copies or downloads the module into `.terraform/modules`. The plan is the proof the refactor is pure.
